summary.text: Rio Roland is the Democratic candidate for the Montana House of Representatives, District 61, in the November 3, 2026 general election.
According to Ballotpedia, he is an engineer; in a Ballotpedia survey he described working as a senior resource analyst in wind energy and chairing the Bozeman Transportation Advisory Board.

paragraphs.text: Rio Roland earned a high school diploma from Bottineau High School, a bachelor's degree from Oregon State University in 1999 and a graduate degree from the University of Minnesota in 2003, according to Ballotpedia.
In a Ballotpedia survey, he said he was born in Bottineau County, North Dakota, lives in Bozeman, and holds a degree in bioresource research and a master's in urban and regional planning.
He said he has built wind farms for 18 years and works as a senior resource analyst for wind energy at Innergex Renewable Energy, after earlier work as a watershed and environmental planner.
Roland said he chairs the Bozeman Transportation Advisory Board and served on the executive committee of the Gallatin County Democrats for two and a half years.
He ran in the Democratic primary for Montana House District 62 in 2024 and lost to Josh Seckinger.
His listed campaign priorities include repealing the 2021 ban on inclusionary zoning, expanding health coverage access, and regulating data centers while promoting renewable energy and transmission.
